newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks to rally if right wins - report.
newsitem.headline: French stocks to rally if right wins - report.

text.p: The Paris bourse will rally if the ruling Conservative coalition wins an upcoming parliamentary election, and the blue-chip CAC-40 index could slide below 2,400 if the Socialists come out ahead, according to Paris consultants Jacques Chahine Finance.

The French stockmarket's underlying fundamentals are strong, reflected by upward revisions in corporate earnings estimates since December, it said in a report. Assuming steady interest rates, the CAC is seen rising this year to around 2,870 points.
"Unfortunately we're going to have to wait and see what happens with the elections," director Jacques Chahine said.

"If the right wins, the stockmarket could jump between five and six percent in a single session," he said. "But if the left wins, we risk seeing negative effects not just in France but in all of Europe. The stakes in this election are high -- for Europe, and for the single currency."
The May 25-June 1 election may turn into a referendum on the single currency as the Socialists are campaigning against further austerity to meet the Maastricht criteria for European monetary union.
Chahine said a Socialist victory could boost French interest rates by a full percentage point right away which would drive the CAC index below 2,400 points.

The CAC, which weakened last week on a poll predicting a tight race, was bolstered on Monday by two polls giving the centre-right a comfortable lead. It was up 10.29 points, or 0.41 percent, at 2,546.55 at 0940 GMT.

A Sofres poll published in Monday's Le Figaro sees the centre-right winning 329 seats, the Socialists, other left and ecologists obtaining 202, the Communists 23 and the National Front one of 555 seats.
An IFOP poll published on Sunday in the Journal du Dimanche showed the RPR-UDF coalition and conservative allies winning between 311 and 331 National Assembly seats.
Brokers say the market will be driven by polls until the election.

But Chahine said there were advantages to President Jacques Chirac's call for a snap election ahead of the March 1998 deadline. "It's far preferable to get the elections over with than to go through a year of campaigning during which political decisions would be frozen," the report said.
It said the bourse was also underpinned by upward revisions in corporate earnings in continental Europe while estimates for U.S. and British groups are on the decline.
Combined profit for the CAC 40 companies should total 114 billion francs ($19.5 billion) for 1997, up 25 percent from 1996 levels, according to the consensus estimates compiled by the firm.
"The median price-earnings ratio of the CAC-40 is at 17.6 times 1997 earnings and offers a 12 percent discount relative to the (German) DAX," the report said.
If the estimates are borne out, the 1998 objective for the CAC-40 index would be 3,377 points, the report said.
